title: Median or average? Reporting weekly sales
summary: Spot when one unusual week distorts the average, and choose the figure that tells the truth about a typical week.

blocks.text: The Nakuru store manager says the store sells about KES 170K a week. You look at the weekly figures and see that nearly every week is close to KES 120K. One week had a huge bulk school order.
The average is being pulled up by that one week. The median, the middle value, is not. You will work out both, measure the gap and let a formula pick the fairer figure to report.

items: Objective: compare AVERAGE and MEDIAN and decide which one to report.
You pass the mission at 75% or more in the Assessment.

blocks.text: AVERAGE adds up all the values and divides by how many there are. One very large value pulls the average upwards, so it can describe a week that never really happened.
Adds the eight weekly sales and divides by 8.
Puts the values in order and picks the middle one. With an even number of values, MEDIAN returns the mean of the two middle values. Excel sorts for you.

blocks.caption: Worked example: five weeks of sales in K
rows: Sorted: 40, 41, 42, 43, 300. The middle one is the third.

blocks.text: Tip: a value far away from all the others is called an outlier. When the average and median are far apart, an outlier is usually the reason. Report the median for a typical week, and mention the outlier separately.
If the gap between average and median (E4) is more than the skew limit (E5) times the median (E3), report the median. Otherwise the average is safe to report.
Keep the limit in its own cell (E5) instead of typing 0.1 inside the formula. Then the rule can be changed in one place. A percentage is stored as a decimal: 10% is 0.1.
Four questions on average and median. Type numbers without commas, for example 125.

items: AVERAGE adds everything and divides by the count, so outliers pull it.
MEDIAN returns the middle value, or the mean of the two middle values when the count is even.
A big gap between average and median is a warning sign of an outlier.
Keep rules such as the skew limit in a cell and point the formula at it.

blocks.text: Next: sell-through %, to see how fast each style is moving.

items.prompt: Weekly sales in K for five weeks are 12, 15, 11, 90 and 14. What is the MEDIAN, in K?
Weekly sales in K for four weeks are 100, 120, 130 and 900. What is the MEDIAN, in K?
A store sells about KES 120K in most weeks, but one week had a KES 540K bulk order. Which figure best describes a typical week?

options.label: The average, because it uses every week
The median, because the bulk order does not drag it upwards
The maximum, because it shows what the store can do
The total, because it is the largest number

items.prompt: In a list of eight weekly sales, the biggest value is changed from 540 to 5,400. What happens?

options.label: Both the average and the median rise a lot
The average rises a lot, but the median stays the same
The median rises a lot, but the average stays the same
